maya: Quick Q about the prompt/prefix caching contract — how should clients detect cache hits for streaming responses? We're prototyping an `X-RW-Cache: hit|miss` header but worried about streaming where headers arrive before any tokens. Also: what should go into the canonical cache key (model id, model_version, prefix hash, full prompt hash?). cc @arjun @ben

arjun: For streaming, header is fine for non-SSE clients. For streaming over SSE/HTTP2/Chunked we should also emit a short control event as the first chunk so clients that only parse body can still see the hit.

arjun: Suggested canonical key: `model_id:version|prefix_sha256|prompt_trunc_sha256` — include model_version to avoid cross-version collisions. Keep prefix truncated to N bytes to avoid huge keys.

ben: Agreed on including model_version. Also +1 on having both header and first-chunk marker. Example we use in tests:
```http
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
X-RW-Cache: hit
Cache-Control: public, max-age=86400
Content-Type: text/event-stream

event: cache
data: {"status":"hit","key":"m_v1:abc123"}

event: tokens
data: {"chunk":"Hello"}
```

ben: For backcompat, older clients that expect `X-Cache-Hit: 1` should still work; we can emit both `X-Cache-Hit: 1` and `X-RW-Cache: hit` during a transitional window.

sam: Quick question on invalidation — if we roll a new quantized model artifact that is semantically equivalent but different weights, do we want to invalidate cache automatically? I'm leaning yes: include quantized_artifact_id or model_build_id in the key.

arjun: Yes. Anything that can affect tokenization or output determinism should be part of the key. So `model_version` should be the full build id for Private/Dedicated tiers. Hosted can optionally map stable aliases to the same cache bucket.

maya: What about clients relying on header-only checks to decide UI badges ("cached reply")? Is header presence guaranteed before any body arrives in all transports?

arjun: Not guaranteed for chunked transfer if proxies buffer. That's why the first-chunk `event: cache` is recommended. Header-first is common, but clients should fall back to the body marker.

ops-bot: Spec doc updated: https://go/internal/api/cache-contract (edited) :white_check_mark:

maya: Outstanding: I'll update the API contract PR to: (1) emit `X-RW-Cache` and legacy `X-Cache-Hit` for 6 weeks, (2) include `model_version`/`model_build_id` in key, (3) add first-chunk SSE/event `event: cache` for streaming, (4) add example responses + tests. PTAL when I put up PR.

ben: Also add one test for client-side parsing when a proxy reorders headers/chunks — simulate slow header delivery.

maya: Thanks — will add that test. @sam can you confirm whether Dedicated needs different retention rules (TTL) vs Hosted?

sam: Dedicated: customers can opt into long-lived cache buckets; default TTL is 7 days but configurable. Hosted: default 1 day. I'll add config knobs to the spec.

maya: Great, thanks all. I'll post PR link here when ready. :rocket:
